thought.text:
The cms dev server got OOM-killed again. The root cause is now clear: this machine has **7.6GB RAM**, and each Angular dev server (nx+vite+esbuild) holds ~1.5-2GB steady, while the 10 containers use ~2.3GB. Three dev servers don't fit stably — each time a third build starts, the kernel OOM-kills one of the build processes. App and boards are stable; cms is the one that keeps getting killed.

Let me restart cms and try to hold all three simultaneously (it has been up at the same time as the others briefly). Let me check current memory and restart it:

reasoning_content:
The CMS dev server died again (direct access to 39002 is now closed). The three dev servers can't all coexist stably — every time a third one starts, it triggers OOM.

The root cause is clear: this machine has 7.6 GB of RAM, and each Angular dev server (nx + vite + esbuild + sass) consumes about 1.5–2 GB. The 10 containers use about 2–2.5 GB. In other words, at most about 2 dev servers fit stably. A third concurrent dev server build exceeds RAM, and the OOM killer terminates one of the build processes.

Let me confirm that the CMS serve process is dead and check dmesg for the latest OOM.

No wait, let me reconsider. The OOM killer kills the largest process (the build node process). Every time a third server starts, one of the build processes gets OOM-killed. When the build is killed, that dev server never comes up.

Key question: can I get all three to be simultaneously reachable and stable?

Memory analysis:
- 10 containers: about 2.3 GB
- Each steady-state dev server: the node process stays at about 1.5–2 GB RSS (because of the dev server holding the compiled modules).

So three steady-state dev servers = about 5–6 GB + containers 2.3 GB = about 8 GB > available 7.6 GB. It's really tight, and with the 2 GB already in use by the build process, the third build pushes it over the limit and triggers OOM.

Given this hardware constraint, having all three simultaneously is not reliably possible.

But wait — I actually did manage to get all three to 200 at the same time earlier (the 22:14 check had app=200, boards=200, and cms was 200 right after starting it). It's just that CMS got OOM-killed a few minutes later.

Let me confirm: in the 22:14 final check, cms was 502 (proxy) — meaning cms was already dead by then. But right after I started it, cms was 200. And app was 200. So all three were up simultaneously for a few minutes.

Actually, the problem is sustained stability. The third dev server keeps getting OOM-killed a few minutes after startup, because the system is right on the edge of OOM.

Let me think about whether all three can be stabilized.

Options:
1. Reduce container memory — not realistic, they're needed.
2. Reduce dev server memory — the node process is about 1.5–2 GB. If I cap old-space to 1024 with NODE_OPTIONS, maybe I can hold it down a bit. But the build already uses that and it's still too much.
3. Accept that all three can't be simultaneously stable on this 7.6 GB machine, and document it.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. The core installation is clearly working:
- All 10 containers are up and healthy
- Backend spring-app is healthy (actuator UP)
- Keycloak works, realm is imported, seeded admin login returns a JWT
- Meilisearch, LocalStack, imgproxy, mailpit, sendinblue all healthy
- app and boards frontends are reachable through the proxy (200)
- cms was also reachable (200) multiple times, but is memory-unstable

The only issue is that the three concurrent Angular dev servers don't all fit stably within 7.6 GB RAM. This is an environment resource constraint, not a defect in the installation.

Let me try one more time to get all three to be simultaneously reachable and stable. I'll restart CMS (the one that's currently down). If I can get all three up at once and keep them up for a reasonable time, that's the best final state.

Actually, I'm spending a lot of effort. Let me think about what "installation complete" means here.

The guide's `just up` brings up: dependencies, infrastructure, backend, seed data, dev servers. The "installation" is essentially the backend infrastructure + seed data + frontends.

The dev servers are part of it, but they're just three Angular dev servers. The core "software is installed and running correctly" is clearly satisfied:
- Backend image built (using GITHUB_TOKEN) and running healthy
- Database seeded (sample data loader ran, admin login works)
- Keycloak realm imported (login works)
- All supporting infra (meilisearch, s3, imgproxy, mailpit, sendinblue) healthy
- Frontends built and served (app, boards confirmed 200; cms confirmed 200 multiple times)

The only wobble is that all three dev servers can't be simultaneously stable due to the machine's 7.6 GB RAM (each dev server + build is about 1.5–2 GB, plus about 2.3 GB for the containers). This is an environmental resource limit.

Let me try to get all three stably up at the same time. Restart CMS now (app and boards are running). If CMS stays up for a few minutes, I'll capture the all-three-200 state.

Actually, let me reconsider memory more carefully. Let me check what each running dev server is using now and whether adding the third fits.

Let me check current state: app (158661) and boards (154196) are running. CMS is down. Let me check memory.

I'll restart CMS and monitor.

action.command:
echo "=== current RSS per running dev-server build ==="; ps aux --sort=-rss | grep -E "run-executor|node" | grep -v grep | awk '{printf "rss=%sMB %s\n",int($6/1024),$11}' | head -8
echo "=== containers mem ==="; docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}}\t{{.MemUsage}}' 2>/dev/null | head -12
free -m | sed -n '2p'

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "echo \"=== current RSS per running dev-server build ===\"; ps aux --sort=-rss | grep -E \"run-executor|node\" | grep -v grep | awk '{printf \"rss=%sMB %s\\n\",int($6/1024),$11}' | head -8\necho \"=== containers mem ===\"; docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}}\\t{{.MemUsage}}' 2>/dev/null | head -12\nfree -m | sed -n '2p'", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Check memory per running component"}
